rationale: Both major findings (CR-001, CR-002) were fixed and verified by the test suite (14 passed). CR-001 resolved by adding _is_parallel_supervisor_handoff_message in history.py: supervisor AIMessages with >1 all-transfer_to_* tool_calls are now skipped in _process_handoff_message before reaching filtered_messages, so the sanitizer never fires the spurious consecutive_assistant_tool_calls WARNING on normal parallel-handoff traffic. CR-002 resolved by adding test_strip_handoff_back_messages_pre_model_hook_sanitizes_orphan_tool_calls_when_filter_is_noop: verifies that an orphan AIMessage with an unmatched tool_call is stripped and the function returns sanitized messages rather than {}; removing the sanitize call would cause filtered_messages == messages and return {} instead, failing the assertion. Confidence remains low: no spec/story was provided so the acceptance lens did not run.

findings.title: Spurious WARNING emitted on every parallel handoff completion
findings.problem: sanitize_rich_history_for_llm is invoked after the handoff filter appends reconstructed single-tool-call AIMessages. The sanitizer encounters the original multi-tool-call supervisor AIMessage followed by reconstructed messages, classifies it as a malformed consecutive-assistant-tool-calls block, drops it correctly, but emits WARNING: 'Dropping malformed assistant tool-call replay block'. This is intended, correct behavior being misclassified as malformed.
findings.impact: Every parallel subagent invocation fires a spurious WARNING in production logs. Monitoring alerts keying on WARNING lines trigger on normal traffic, masking real malformed-sequence warnings and creating alert fatigue that degrades incident response.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish expected parallel-handoff drops from genuinely malformed sequences. Either log at DEBUG when the drop is a known transformation, or mark messages the handoff filter intentionally supersedes so the sanitizer can skip the WARNING for those.

findings.title: No test for primary sanitization fix path (handoff filter is a no-op)
findings.problem: The new test exercises the parallel handoff path where sanitize_rich_history_for_llm acts as a side-effect of handoff reconstruction. There is no test where the handoff filter makes no changes but the input contains an orphan AIMessage with unmatched tool_calls — the direct sanitization scenario the fix is intended to handle.
findings.impact: A regression removing or short-circuiting the sanitize call (e.g., an early return inserted above line 209) would not be caught. The primary bug fix remains unverified by the test suite.
findings.recommendation: Add a test: input messages contain an AIMessage with one or more tool_calls but no subsequent matching ToolMessage (an orphan call) and no handoff-back markers. Assert the function returns {'llm_input_messages': [...]} with the orphan AIMessage stripped (or reconstructed as a valid pair), rather than returning {}.
